reason: Yahweh explicitly expresses displeasure with the people of Nineveh at the outset of this passage. In Jonah 1:2, God states that the people's wickedness has 'come up before me' (עָלְתָה רָעָתָם לְפָנַי), and commands Jonah to 'cry out against' (קְרָא עָלֶיהָ) the city. Throughout the narrative, Yahweh references their 'evil' (רָעָה) and violence (חָמָס). Even at the passage's conclusion, God acknowledges His concern for the large population while withholding judgment. This constitutes a clear complaint about the people's conduct and moral condition.
